test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 13 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

This is __the most toughest exam __that I have ever taken.
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. the toughest exam .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"most"** is used to form the superlative degree of adjectives, but it cannot be paired with an adjective that is already in its superlative form, such as **"toughest."**
 
• The correct form is simply **"the toughest exam"** without the word **"most."**
 
• Using **"most toughest"** is redundant and grammatically incorrect.

Correct sentence: *This is the toughest exam that I have ever taken.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superlative Degree:**

 
 
• **Definition:** Used to compare three or more things, showing the highest degree of the quality being described.
 
• **Example:** "This is the tallest building in the city."
 
• **Rule:** Do not use "most" with adjectives that already have superlative forms ending in "-est" (e.g., tallest, smartest, toughest).
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Redundancy: Using both "most" and the "-est" form together (e.g., "most fastest").
 
• Incorrect pairing of comparative and superlative forms.
